q: Scientists can use genetically modified organisms to profile the DNA sequence of a _____ tumour.
e: Scientists can use genetically modified organisms to profile the DNA sequence of a cancerous tumour. Cancerous is the word, not benign or viral.

q: Genetic engineering is the alteration of the _____ material of an organism in a specific manner.
e: Genetic engineering is the alteration of the genetic material of an organism in a specific manner. So we write genetic. Leave protein and cellular out.

q: Transgenic bacteria, plants, and animals are commonly referred to as genetically modified organisms, or _____.
e: Transgenic bacteria, plants, and animals are commonly referred to as genetically modified organisms, or GMOs. So we write GMOs. Leave DNA and RNA out.

q: A transgenic organism is produced from the introduction of foreign DNA into its genome, providing it with a new _____.
e: A transgenic organism is produced from the introduction of foreign DNA into its genome, providing it with a new phenotype. The blank is phenotype. Not genotype or karyotype.

q: Recombinant DNA is a method of transferring a gene into the genome of another organism of different _____.
e: Recombinant DNA is a method of transferring a gene into the genome of another organism of different species. The blank is species. Not genus or family.

q: In order to insert the recombinant gene into a target cell, a _____ is needed.
e: In order to insert the recombinant gene into a target cell, a vector is needed. So we write vector. Leave enzyme and primer out.

q: Which of the following can be used as a vector to insert recombinant DNA?
e: The answer is plasmid. Transgenic animals can be used to produce pharmaceutical products such as human proteins by using a recombinant plasmid vector. Not ribosome or lysosome.

q: Vitamin A deficiency can cause blindness and an _____ deficiency syndrome.
e: Vitamin A deficiency can cause blindness and an immune deficiency syndrome. The blank is immune. Not enzyme or protein.

q: The genes for beta-carotene in Golden Rice come from daffodils and _____ bacteria.
e: The genes for beta-carotene in Golden Rice come from daffodils and erwinia bacteria. Erwinia is the word, not E. coli or streptococcus.

q: The genes for making beta-carotene are inserted into plasmids that occur inside _____.
e: The genes for making beta-carotene are inserted into plasmids that occur inside bacillus. So we write bacillus. Leave agrobacterium and E. coli out.

q: Agrobacteria are added to a petri dish containing rice _____.
e: Agrobacteria are added to a petri dish containing rice seed. So we write seed. Leave leaf and embryo out.

q: Substituting the gene from daffodils plant with one from _____ gave higher quantities of carotene.
e: Substituting the gene from daffodils plant with one from maize gave higher quantities of carotene. So we write maize. Leave wheat and rice out.

q: Golden Rice contains the orange pigment _____ which can be converted into vitamin A.
e: Golden Rice contains the orange pigment beta-carotene which can be converted into vitamin A. So we write beta-carotene. Leave chlorophyll and xanthophyll out.

q: One benefit of genetic engineering of crops is increased resistance to pests and _____.
e: One benefit of genetic engineering of crops is increased resistance to pests and pathogens. Pathogens is the word, not herbicides or fertilizers.

q: Genetic engineering of crops can lead to enhanced food quality due to slower _____.
e: Genetic engineering of crops can lead to enhanced food quality due to slower spoilage. Spoilage is the word, not growth or ripening.

q: Since the mid-1980s, medicinal products such as human growth hormone and _____ have been produced in transgenic plants.
e: Since the mid-1980s, medicinal products such as human growth hormone and antibodies have been produced in transgenic plants. So we write antibodies. Leave lipids and sugars out.

q: One type of antibody made by transgenic corn can deliver _____ to tumour cells.
e: One type of antibody made by transgenic corn can deliver radioisotopes to tumour cells. So we write radioisotopes. Leave antibiotics and vitamins out.

q: An antibody made by transgenic soybeans can be used to treat genital _____.
e: An antibody made by transgenic soybeans can be used to treat genital herpes. The blank is herpes. Not warts or cancer.

q: To produce transgenic animals, a foreign gene is inserted into the genome of an animal _____ that is then fertilized.
e: To produce transgenic animals, a foreign gene is inserted into the genome of an animal oocyte that is then fertilized. So we write oocyte. Leave sperm and zygote out.

q: After the oocyte is fertilized, it is implanted in a host female and allowed to _____.
e: After the oocyte is fertilized, it is implanted in a host female and allowed to develop. The blank is develop. Not divide or mutate.

q: Transgenic animals can produce human proteins using a recombinant _____ vector.
e: Transgenic animals can produce human proteins using a recombinant plasmid vector. The blank is plasmid. Not viral or lipid.

q: The vector contains a promoter that directs the expression of the genes in _____ cells.
e: The vector contains a promoter that directs the expression of the genes in mammary cells. Mammary is the word, not muscle or nerve.

q: In the production of GM sheep, the human hormone gene is cloned next to a sheep _____ promoter.
e: In the production of GM sheep, the human hormone gene is cloned next to a sheep insulin promoter. The blank is insulin. Not growth hormone or  eta-lactoglobulin.

q: GM animals can be used for the production of organs for transplantation, known as _____.
e: GM animals can be used for the production of organs for transplantation, known as xero-transplantation. Xero-transplantation is the word, not cloning or biopsy.
